extracted.intended_audience: policy makers, patent office analysts, IP statisticians, researchers and IP professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, metrics and methodological standards for measuring and comparing patenting activity (filings, pendency, oppositions, costs, specialization) across countries, technologies and offices. Includes IPC-to-technology concordance and cost-methodology assumptions used for comparative analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology-field patent filings (energy technologies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent filings related to solar (thermal and photo), fuel cell and wind energy are identified based on International Patent Classification (IPC) symbols assigned to patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IPC-based definitions (see Annex B) to classify filings into solar, fuel cell and wind energy technology groups. Interpret distribution of applications by country of origin as indicating concentration of research activities in these technologies; compare absolute volumes (e.g. total wind filings considerably less than solar and fuel cell). See annex B for detailed IPC symbol lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent filings per gross domestic product (resident filings/GDP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratio of resident patent filings to GDP to correct for the effects of country size and improve comparability across countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation notes: the ratio reduces country-size distortion observed in raw resident filings. Example: the gap between Republic of Korea and Japan is smaller under this indicator than for raw resident filings. Time comparisons can show whether patenting intensity grows faster than GDP (e.g., China and Republic of Korea had higher 2006 ratios than 2000). Use GDP in billions of constant US$ based on PPPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent filings per million population (resident filings/population)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident filings per million population to normalize filings by population size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ratio generally follows the resident filings/GDP pattern but may reorder countries with very large populations (e.g., China, India, Russian Federation rank lower here than under filings/GDP). Use to compare per-capita patenting activity and detect notable increases/decreases over time (e.g., increases in Republic of Korea, USA, New Zealand, China; decreases in Japan, Sweden, Finland).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent filings per research and development expenditure (patent intensity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident filings divided by R&D expenditure (patent intensity). R&D expenditures are in millions of constant US$ based on PPPs and are lagged by 2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High patent intensity indicates a high level of patenting relative to R&D investment. Use lagged R&D (2-year lag) to better align inputs and outputs. Examples: Republic of Korea, Russian Federation, Japan, China and New Zealand have high patent intensity. Note strong correlation between R&D and patent filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trends in resident filings per R&D expenditure
rubrics_metrics.description: Time series analysis of patent intensity to detect increases or declines by country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret changes as due to relative growth rates of resident filings versus R&D expenditure. Examples: China and India saw slight increases (higher growth in filings relative to R&D); Germany, Japan and the UK showed declines largely due to falling resident filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending patent applications by patent office
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of patent applications waiting for substantive examination at a patent office (pending applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of office-specific definitions and data comparability issues. Pending counts depend on workload and resources and on procedural rules (e.g., change in JPO request-for-examination rule shortened from 7 to 3 years in 2004, affecting counts). Example: USPTO had in excess of 1 million pending applications in 2006.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency time metrics (first office action, total pendency, pendency in examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time delays measured as time to first office action, total pendency time, and pendency time in examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare offices using the same metric but interpret cautiously due to differences in office procedures and measurement. Examples: EPO has highest average total pendency time (total pendency ≈ twice first office action pendency); KIPO has lowest first office action pendency and has decreased over 1999–2006. Chart both first action and total/examination pendency for fuller view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability caveat for office metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Data presented for different patent offices may not be comparable due to specificities of each office (workload, resources, procedural rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly note procedural differences (e.g., request-for-examination timing) when comparing counts or pendency between offices; consider harmonizing definitions or annotating comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and naming differences for opposition/invalidation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Different offices use different terms and procedures for post-grant challenges: 'opposition' (Germany, EPO, Korea), 'Re-examination' (USA), 'Invalidation Request' (China), 'Trial for invalidation' (Japan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When compiling cross-office statistics, map local procedure names to a common concept (post-grant challenge) and annotate methodological differences. Note that Chinese data are estimated for some years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistics on opposition/invalidation requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of patents subjected to an opposition/invalidation request relative to patents granted for the same year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reported offices, requests typically constitute less than 6% of total patents granted (less than 1% for most large offices; EPO is exception). Trends may indicate increasing interest of third parties in challenging grants. Interpret sudden changes in counts with reference to procedural changes (e.g., JPO change in 2003).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost of patenting component breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent cost estimates decomposed into official fees, maintenance, legal costs, translation costs, and other direct costs for scenarios (2, 7, 15 countries / PCT vs direct filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated shares indicate translation costs can be 18–36% of total depending on number of countries; official fees ≈ one-third of total; legal costs vary from ~25% to >50% depending on countries selected. Costs based on Global IP Estimator typical fee schedules; actual costs vary widely by options chosen and jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patenting cost scenarios and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost scenarios (2, 7, 15 countries) assume an applicant that is a large company based in the USA, filing electronically when possible; priority year 2006; last maintenance year 2016; patent application has 30 pages (2 drawings), 15 claims, 2 convention priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology excludes in-house and pre-filing costs. No legal costs counted for USPTO procedure (assumed applicant can proceed without external support). ISA selection depends on scenario (USPTO or EPO). No Chapter II demand in the scenarios. List of countries for each scenario provided in Annex D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patenting cost methodology (Annex D): included/excluded stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost estimations include filing, examining, prosecution and granting stages and the international phase for PCT scenarios; do not include in-house and pre-filing costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global IP bases legal and translation cost estimates on typical fee schedules supplied by foreign associates. All figures in US dollars. Use these methodological notes when interpreting or reproducing cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC (International Patent Classification) to technology concordance
rubrics_metrics.description: A concordance table mapping IPC symbols (sections, classes, subclasses and groups) to fields of technology (I-V and subfields).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the concordance (Annex B) to group patent data into technology fields (electrical engineering, instruments, chemistry, mechanical engineering, other fields). For energy technology definitions, specific IPC symbol lists are provided for solar, fuel cells and wind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy technology IPC definitions (solar, fuel cells, wind)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed IPC symbol lists defining solar energy (solar photovoltaic and solar thermal), fuel cells, and wind energy technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact IPC subgroup lists shown (Annex B) to classify patent families into these energy subfields to ensure consistent cross-country comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Specialization Index (RSI)
rubrics_metrics.description: RSI = country's share of foreign-oriented patent families in a specific technology / country's share in all foreign-oriented patent families. Positive RSI implies relatively high share in that technology; negative RSI implies relatively low share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RSI to indicate a country's R&D strength in a particular field. Compute using F(c,t) = number of filings/patent families in technology t and country c; compare across countries and technologies. Reported as numeric index values (positive/negative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual or company that files an application for patent rights. The name of the patent applicant is used to determine the owner of the patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application (Filing) Date (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date on which the patent office received the patent application that meets the minimum requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country of Origin (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The country of residence of the first-named applicant or assignee of a patent application; used to determine the origin of the patent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: European Patent Convention (EPC) (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Convention on the Grant of European Patents, instituting the European Patent Organization and providing a legal system under which European patents are granted; permits a single application at the EPO designating EPC Member States.

rubrics_metrics.name: European Patent Office (EPO) (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A regional patent office created under the EPC, responsible for granting European patents for EPC Member States; also acts as an International Searching Authority and International Preliminary Examining Authority for the PCT and performs searches for some national offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extra-Regional Filings (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications by applicants who are not resident of a member State of a region (such as the EPC) filed at Offices of that region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-Oriented Patent Families (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of inter-related patent applications filed in one or more foreign countries to protect the same invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Date (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date on which the patent office granted patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A measure of national income and output for a country's economy; used in ratios (e.g., resident filings/GDP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GDP data in the report are in billions of constant US dollars based on PPPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau (IB) (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IB of WIPO acts as the receiving Office for PCT international applicants and handles processing tasks; publishes international applications 18 months after filing or priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Patent Classification (IPC) (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: An internationally recognized hierarchical patent classification system dividing technology into sections, classes, subclasses and groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Annex B for IPC-to-technology mappings used in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intra-Regional Filings (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications by applicants who are resident of a member State of a region filed at offices of the same region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The process by which patent protection is maintained, usually by paying maintenance (renewal) fees at regular intervals; failure to pay may cause lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cost scenarios assume last maintenance year 10 years from filing; maintenance costs may be included or excluded in specific breakdowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Resident Filings (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed at the Office of a State where the first-named applicant does not have residence; used to compile non-resident patent statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an American applicant filing at JPO is a non-resident filing for JPO statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrative process for disputing the validity of a granted patent, often limited to a specific time period after grant (e.g., up to nine months for European patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different jurisdictions have varied procedures and names for post-grant challenges; map them when comparing data across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paris Convention / Right of Priority (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international treaty establishing the right of priority allowing a patent applicant to claim priority for up to 12 months when filing in other contracting states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Application (procedure) (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for requesting patent protection at a patent office: applicant files application and fees, office examines and decides whether to grant or reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international treaty administered by WIPO enabling applicants to seek patent protection simultaneously in many countries by filing a single 'international application' with a receiving Office; PCT does not grant patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT simplifies multinational filings by delaying national phase entry decisions; national/regional offices decide on grants in their jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Family (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of inter-related patent applications filed in one or more countries to protect the same invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Grant (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal rights conferred by a patent office on the applicant for a limited period (normally 20 years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent in Force (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent that is currently valid; to remain in force it must be maintained by paying fees at regular intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: An exclusive right granted by law to applicants/assignees to make use of and exploit their inventions for a limited period (generally 20 years from filing); in return the applicant must disclose the invention so skilled persons can replicate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent system balances exclusive rights and public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT International Application (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application filed under the PCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT National Phase Entry (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A PCT international application which has entered the national/regional phase, usually within 30 months from the priority date (longer in some offices), requiring explicit action and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending Application (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application waiting for substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication Date (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date on which the patent application is published (normally 18 months after filing or priority date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional Application (Grant) (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application (or granted patent) filed (granted) by a regional patent office (e.g., EPO, ARIPO, EAPO, OAPI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and Development Expenditure (glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Money spent on systematic creative work to increase stock of knowledge; used as denominator in patent intensity calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the report R&D expenditure figures are in millions of constant US$ based on PPPs and are lagged by 2 years for resident filings/R&D ratios.
